qt: to the Commission Nikolaos Anadiotis (NI) Subject:

The EU-India Free Trade Agreement provides for reciprocal tariff concessions with different implications for the sectors involved1. The Commission has highlighted the opportunities the agreement will create in the transport services sector and for agri-food products, namely olive oil, wine and kiwis, by significantly reducing Indian tariffs2. By contrast, the Greek clothing and textile sector may face more intense competition within the EU. In 2025, 75 % of Greek clothing exports and 68 % of textile exports went to the EU3. India’s clothing and textile exports to the EU totalled EUR 4.5 billion and EUR 2.7 billion respectively4 and the agreement widens its market access5. The agreement also provides for a seasonal duty free quota of 85 000 tonnes of Indian table grapes6. The seasonal nature of the quota limits overlap with the main Greek marketing year, without ruling out consequences for prices or individual markets7. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What is the estimated net impact of the agreement, especially on the Greek economy and employment by sector?
For which Greek products does it estimate a loss of market share within the EU due to more favourable Indian imports and what is the estimated cost for Greek producers?
What indicators will it monitor for the prompt activation of the bilateral safeguard clause in the Greek sectors that are the most exposed?
